content: MAC address first octet's low-order bits: bit 0 (I/G, least significant bit of first byte) = 0 unicast / 1 multicast; bit 1 (U/L) = 0 universally administered (vendor OUI burned-in) / 1 locally administered (software-assigned, includes randomized MACs). A device performing MAC randomization forces U/L=1 and I/G=0, which always makes the second hex nibble one of {2,6,A,E} - this is the standard heuristic for randomized/private MAC detection, but it is a heuristic (locally-administered does not always mean randomized; VMs and manually-set MACs also set this bit).
